properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here: the enum and the offer list are first-party code. The wallet server negotiates a symmetric session cipher with the TAS by offering ALL SymmetricCipherType values (EnrollEntityServiceImpl.java:193-195 Candidate.builder().ciphers(Arrays.asList(SymmetricCipherType.values()))), so ECB modes are genuinely offered to the peer. mergeSharedSecretAndNonce (BaseCryptoUtil.java:170-171) then sizes the SHA-256-derived session key for the negotiated cipher. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here. CBC is the expected session cipher and the wallet-at-rest cipher; both are unauthenticated (no MAC/HMAC anywhere in this repo), so the D-rated ECB offer is the most urgent part of this posture. The wallet file holds every DID private key of this server.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here. secp256k1 is a supported-but-not-default curve in this deployment: wallet keygen uses SECP256r1 (BaseWalletUtil.java:118), and the ECDH enrollment hardcodes SECP_256_R1, so secp256k1 remains protocol surface for DID documents from other entities. Migration to ML-DSA/SLH-DSA would retire both curves' signature use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here. secp256r1 is the primary curve of this deployment: wallet keygen (BaseWalletUtil.java:118, CryptoKeyPairInfo.KeyAlgorithmType.SECP256r1), Secp256r1Signature2018 proofs on all signing requests, and the ephemeral ECDH keypair for TAS enrollment (EnrollEntityServiceImpl.java:101-103). Shor-recoverable signatures and key agreement. The two fixture sites are sample/test-only and do not carry the object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Observable here, changeable in this repo: the endpoints and the curve offered are first-party. The actual quantum-vulnerable key agreement (ephemeral P-256 keypair + CryptoUtils.generateSharedSecret + SHA-256 KDF) is reported as a separate ecdh_dh_agreement finding at EnrollEntityServiceImpl.java:271 since these two sites only name the protocol.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here: the offer list could drop AES-128 (and ECB) at the enum. Grover leaves AES-128 a 64-bit quantum margin — not urgent, below CNSA 2.0.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here. This is a raw single-pass hash used as a KDF (no HKDF salt/info, no domain separation) — acceptable today, worth noting it feeds the AES session key for VC decryption. Note the SHA-256 use for admin PASSWORD hashing on the frontend (crypto-js, sha256-hash.ts) is a separate, weaker use reported as its own finding.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here. AES-256 is the strongest option in this repo (A+); the weakness of the wallet encryption is not the key size but the hardcoded password feeding it (reported separately) and CBC/PKCS5 without authentication.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here. java.security.SecureRandom is the platform CSPRNG — adequate; not quantum-fragile in practice. Protocol nonces/IVs additionally come from the omnione SDK (BaseCryptoUtil.generateNonce → CryptoUtils.generateNonce(16), RandomUtil.generateNonce → NonceGenerator.generate16ByteNonce), which are CSPRNG-backed in the SDK.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here (dependency upgrade). crypto-js 4.2.0 is actively used for admin password hashing — the crypto-js SHA-256 password use is reported as its own finding; the library itself also ships MD5/SHA-1/AES-ECB etc., which the image ships regardless of use.
